title: Incident Snapshot — Rapid investigation checklist & SIEM export flow
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact on-call snapshot for security responders: a practical step-by-step checklist to triage incidents, verify RBAC v2 state, pull authoritative audit logs, trigger automated SIEM exports, and capture evidence with minimal context switching. Designed for use in the first 0-60 minutes and as the canonical source when generating the post-incident timeline.

Scope:
- Applicability: infra+control-plane incidents, suspicious auths, privilege anomalies, suspicious service-to-service activity.
- Not for full DFIR forensic deep-dive (use full forensics playbook), but sufficient to preserve evidence and contain.

Quick triage (0–10m):
1) Confirm signal origin: alert id / slack thread / pager notation. Record: alert_id, source_system, detection_rules.
2) Assign incident owner in Slack #sec-oncall and create minimal incident stub: JIRA/SEC-#### or update existing ticket.
3) Snapshot live context: take screenshots of any UI alerts (console, Cloud Console). Copy raw alert JSON to incident ticket.
4) Initial severity decision: P0/P1/P2. If P0, escalate to lead and SRE immediately.

Immediate containment (10–20m):
- If active exfil or privilege escalation suspected: temporarily revoke affected principal tokens via RBAC revoke endpoint (examples below) and rotate service account keys.
- If suspicious host/process: add host to isolation group in inventory and block egress via firewall rule.

RBAC v2 sanity checks (commands):
- Verify membership and recent grants for a principal (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://control-plane.redwood/api/v1/rbac/v2/principals/{principal_id}/effective-roles"
- Confirm no recently-created admin role bindings in last 24h: run audit query (see Audit log retrieval).
- Quick manual checks: list last 50 grant events for a role:
  gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.project_id="redwood-prod" AND protoPayload.methodName:"GrantRole"' --limit 50 --freshness=1d

Audit log retrieval (authoritative):
- Preferred stores: central audit BigQuery dataset (audit_logs.events_*), S3 archive (audit-logs/YYYY/), and SIEM index (splunk: audit_redwood_*).
- Minimum fields to export for incident: timestamp, principal_id, action, resource, outcome, request_id, ip_address, session_id, role_changes, grant_source, trace_id.
- Example BigQuery query (Quick):
  SELECT event_time, principal_id, action, resource, outcome, metadata
  FROM `redwood-prod.audit_logs.events_*`
  WHERE event_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 24 HOUR)
    AND (principal_id = "user:alex@redwood.com" OR request_id = "REDACTED")
  ORDER BY event_time DESC

Automated SIEM export steps (0–30m):
1) Trigger on-call SIEM export job (k8s job: infra/siem-exporter) via runbook job runner or Jenkins. If no UI access, run export lambda:
  aws lambda invoke --function-name evidence-export-lambda --payload '{"query":"<BQ/ES query>", "target":"splunk", "ticket":"JIRA-XXXX"}' /tmp/output.json
2) Include schema mapping: map audit fields to SIEM indices (see field map below). Use --include-raw to preserve original JSON.
3) Verify export arrival in SIEM index (splunk search): index=audit_redwood sourcetype=json earliest=-1h | stats count by principal_id, action

Suggested audit-to-SIEM field map (simple canonical):
- event_time => @timestamp
- principal_id => user.id
- action => event.action
- resource => resource.name
- outcome => event.outcome
- ip_address => network.client.ip
- request_id => event.request_id
- role_changes => event.changes.roles
- k8s_pod => container.pod.name

Evidence collection checklist (preserve, do not mutate):
- Export raw audit log window (min 24–72h) to immutable storage (s3://sec-evidence/incident-<id>/raw/).
- Archive relevant console recordings, snapshots, AMI IDs, container images.
- Preserve KV cache access logs (serving runtime) if model-level activity suspected.
- If legal hold needed, annotate ticket and set evidence retention TTL to indefinite.

Chain-of-custody notes:
- All evidence picks must be recorded in ticket with who/when/why and S3 path.
- Avoid local copies on personal laptops. Use evidence-export-lambda and role-based write-only artifact bucket.

Post-incident template (fill by end of 72h):
- Title: short description
- Impact: affected services/users, estimated data scope, customer impact
- Timeline: minute-granular list, include detection point, containment steps, changes made (include request_ids)
- Root cause hypothesis: summary + confidence level
- Remediation & mitigations implemented (short-term fix + engineering backlog items)
- Auditability actions: log schema gaps found, retention changes, RBAC policy adjustments
- Lessons learned & owners for follow-up tasks

Communication & escalation:
- Channel: #sec-oncall for ongoing, #sec-all for 1-hour status, executive@redwood for P0 updates.
- Provide cadence: initial triage (10m), containment update (30m), 1h summary, resolution summary.

After-action metrics to capture:
- Time to detection (alert_time -> triage_start)
- Time to containment (triage_start -> containment_complete)
- Number of principals affected, number of role changes reversed
- Volume of data exported to SIEM/evidence store (GB)

Automation hooks & runbooks referenced:
- evidence-export-lambda (aws account: redwood-prod)
- infra/siem-exporter (k8s job)
- rbac-revoke-service (internal API)
- confluence:SEC-IR-guides-2024 (detailed forensics runbook)
- TODO: link to runbook for on-prem private deployments export (private-deployments section).

Quick reminders / gotchas:
- Don’t delete audit indices; always export first.
- RBAC revokes are broad: prefer scoped temp-deny when possible.
- If external regulator involved, enable chain-of-custody early and notify legal.

Open questions / follow-ups (notes to action):
- Add a canned SIEM dashboard for RBAC v2 anomalies: owner: Marcus Li (action item).
- Validate that evidence-export-lambda preserves original log ordering and request_id (Elena to confirm).
- Evaluate retention increase from 90d -> 180d for audit_logs.events on high-severity customers (exec review).

Appendix: sample SIEM query for suspicious grant events (Splunk-ish):
index=audit_redwood event.action="GrantRole" OR event.action="CreateBinding" | table _time, user.id, event.action, resource.name, event.changes.roles, src_ip | sort -_time

Contact rota: on-call week of 2025-07-21: Asha P. (primary), Marcus L. (secondary), Elena G. (SPOC).

Notes to self: keep this page intentionally short and link to the longer playbooks. Use this as the ‘first run’ checklist — expand into PRD if we adopt the SIEM export pattern permanently.
